###############
### Bigrams ###
###############

```{r}
bigrams <- DTS_fulltext |> 
  unnest_tokens(bigram, sentence, token="ngrams", n=2)

bigrams
```

```{r}
data(stop_words)

bigrams |> 
  filter(!is.na(bigram)) |> 
  separate(bigram, c("word1", "word2"), sep = " ") |> 
  filter(!word1 %in% stop_words$word) |> 
  filter(!word2 %in% stop_words$word) |> 
  count(word1, word2)
```

```{r}
bigram_filtered <- bigrams |> 
  filter(!is.na(bigram)) |> 
  separate(bigram, c("word1", "word2"), sep = " ") |> 
  filter(!word1 %in% stop_words$word) |> 
  filter(!word2 %in% stop_words$word) |> 
  count(word1, word2, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r}
deaf_bigram <- bigram_filtered |> 
  filter(grepl("deaf", word1, ignore.case = TRUE) | grepl("deaf", word2, ignore.case = TRUE))
```


##########################
### Sentiment Analysis ###
##########################

```{r}
DTS_analyze <- DTS_fulltext |> 
  filter(!is.na(sentence)) |> 
  select(sentence, id) |> 
  mutate(id = row_number())
```

```{r}
DTS_sentiment <- DTS_analyze %>%
  get_sentences() %>%
  sentiment_by(by = c("id"))
```

# Describing DTS sentiments in context
```{r}

print(paste0("From this exercise, the most positive sentence in the DTS database was scored at ", max(DTS_sentiment$ave_sentiment), " while the most negative was scored at ", min(DTS_sentiment$ave_sentiment),". For context, the median value was ", median(DTS_sentiment$ave_sentiment), " and the standard deviation was ", sd(DTS_sentiment$ave_sentiment), "."))
        
```


############
### KWIC ###
############

# Getting what we need for tokenization
```{r}
DTS_to_token <- DTS_fulltext |> 
  filter(!is.na(sentence))
```


# Creating corpus for KWIC
```{r}
DTS_corpus <- corpus(DTS_to_token, text_field = "sentence") # build a new corpus from the texts
head(DTS_corpus)
```

# Tokenizing DTS corpus
```{r}
DTS_tokens <- tokens(DTS_corpus)
```


# KWIC
# Phrases taken from own thoughts and above bigram
```{r}
DTS_KWIC <- kwic(DTS_tokens, phrase(c("deaf", "artificial intelligence","AI", "deaf sentiment", "sign", "sign language", "sentiment", "access*", "accessibility solutions", "disabilit*", "hearing", "language barrier", "RIT", "Rochester", "language development", "rylo", "disabled", "communication")), window = 50) |> as.data.frame()
```

# Filtering DTS_KWIC down to just any variation of Artificial intelligence to see how much the term actually relates to the topic at hand. AI is very prevalent in DTS but is it relevant in this dataset?
```{r}
AI_KWIC <- DTS_KWIC |> 
  filter(grepl("Artificial Intelligence", keyword, ignore.case=TRUE) | grepl("AI", keyword, ignore.case=TRUE))
```

######################
### Bigrams Part 2 ###
######################

# Running bigrams on a slightly modified version of DTS_KWIC. My thinking is that if I run bigrams on DTS_KWIC then I'll obtain a bigrams that's much more focused on DTS instead of a bigrams that's filled with nonsense since some of the news articles talk about a bunch of topics and a small section related to DTS, leaving me with a lot of content that doesn't pertain to DTS

# Modifying DTS_KWIC

# Get all unique sentence ids from DTS_KWIC
```{r}
KWIC_IDs <- DTS_KWIC |> 
  select(docname) |> 
  mutate(id = as.numeric(sub("text", "", docname))) |> 
  select(id) |> 
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

# Getting all sentences in DTS_analyze that have an ID that shows up in KWIC_IDs
```{r}
KWIC_to_bigram <- DTS_analyze |> 
  filter(id %in% KWIC_IDs$id)
```

# Now that we have only the sentences which show up in KWIC and ensure that the whole sentence is there. We can now do bigrams on just the KWIC sentences.
```{r}
KWIC_bigram <- KWIC_to_bigram |> 
  unnest_tokens(bigram, sentence, token="ngrams", n=2)
```

```{r}
KWIC_bigram_filtered <- KWIC_bigram |> 
  filter(!is.na(bigram)) |> 
  separate(bigram, c("word1", "word2"), sep = " ") |> 
  filter(!word1 %in% stop_words$word) |> 
  filter(!word2 %in% stop_words$word) |> 
  count(word1, word2, sort = TRUE)
```
